A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same House of Dextra study and retain its methods, experiments, and appendices. Although v5's main-text correlation chart is clipped, the corresponding analysis is available in its appendix, supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v5 reports original simulation experiments, physical robot-hand evaluations, controller comparisons, and morphology sensitivity analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v7 retains these original empirical results, including simulation performance in Table 1, real-world rotation measurements in Table 3, and supplementary experiments in Appendix 9.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same modular morphology grammar, morphology-conditioned PPO policies, GNN-guided search with Gumbel exploration, and blind-policy deployment procedure. Relocated equations and explanations do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate in-hand rotation, tabletop grasping, and flipping using the same object coverage and hand embodiments. The real-world evaluations, LEAP parameter study, and appendix controller test scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains RoboGrammar, Monte Carlo search, the MPPI variant, vision-based single-cube LEAP, blind LEAP, and the version without fine-tuning. Appendix 9.1 retains the same MPPI/CEM and individual-PPO comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain unchanged, including 50 iterations with 40 designs each, 2,048 parallel simulation environments, baseline training conditions, and blind real-world evaluation. Tables 4–5 retain the same physics, actuator, and domain-randomization settings.

E4.justification: The fine-tuning comparison, controller failure cases, cross-embodied versus individual-PPO study, hand morphology comparisons, and parameter sensitivity analyses are unchanged. Repositioning the correlation chart does not introduce an additional analysis.

E5.justification: Figure 5 retains the same shaded bands, and the appendix parameter plots retain their sample-count and correlation annotations. No additional seed information, repeated-run reporting, uncertainty estimates, or statistical testing is introduced.

E6.justification: The tables, plots, and reported findings retain their results. For example, Table 1 reports 3.3 rad/s for the fine-tuned method, 1.85 without fine-tuning, and 0.26 for RoboGrammar in both versions. Real-world measurements and appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The graph and MDP definitions, bi-level optimization formulation, and objectives in Equations 1–10 are unchanged. Equation relocation and typesetting adjustments introduce no mathematical revision, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim scalable cross-embodied co-design, manufacturable modular hands, zero-shot real-world deployment, and an under-24-hour pipeline. The abstract's expanded open-source wording does not alter the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning morphology, controller suitability, and task-specific hand designs remain unchanged. Section 8 retains the limitations involving predefined components, single-task optimization, and omitted compliance, material, and actuation choices.

D1.justification: v7 repeats the project address in the abstract and explicitly mentions open-source generated hands. However, v5 already supplies that address in Section 1 and describes open-source code and designs in Section 10. Implementation and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in the introduction and related-work section are unchanged. Citation and hyperlink formatting changes do not add references or revise relationships to prior research.

P1.justification: The abstract's final sentence is revised to mention generated hands and display the existing project URL. Figure references are adjusted for renumbering, while the substantive prose and section sequence remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from page 4 to page 5. The task illustration moves from page 9 to page 10 and becomes Figure 7; the correlation chart becomes Figure 6 and fits fully on page 9, correcting v5's clipping. Citation and link coloring also changes.

improvement.justification: v7 repairs the clipped correlation chart, making its axes, labels, and caption readable alongside Section 6, and makes the existing project link more prominent in the abstract. Some relocated figures interrupt adjacent prose, but the clipping repair provides a limited net readability gain. Scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
